testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Get both sets of wheels onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: If you drive onto the shoulder to avoid a hazard, stay on it until you stop. Then signal, check your mirrors, and merge back into traffic. Avoid hard braking on the shoulder at speeds above 20 mph. Keep one set of wheels on the pavement if you can.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Place as little weight as possible over the axles.
Place the right amount of weight over the axles.
Not worry about how the weight is distributed.
Only place weight over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Balance the weight of cargo evenly in the trailer. Too much or too little weight on an axle can affect how you control the vehicle. Too much weight on one axle can also damage it.

questions.question: The minimum tread depth for rear tires is:
questions.explanation: Check your tires for depth. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread in every major groove. Rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch of tread. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will:

options.text: Make you stop in a shorter distance.
Not change how you apply the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change how you apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your brakes from locking up during hard braking. You should brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in one without it. ABS does not always shorten your stopping distance.

questions.question: To use stab braking in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes hard until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll again, then repeat.
Press the brakes about halfway and keep the wheels rolling.
Fully press the brakes, let the wheels lock up, and hold the pedal down until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes hard until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll again, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means pressing the brakes hard until they lock. Then release them until the wheels start rolling. Repeat this process.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, you must:
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to transport any hazardous materials that require your vehicle to be placarded.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking to a passenger), or both (like texting on your phone).

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts for tightness and wear. Each belt in your engine has a safe amount of looseness that varies by vehicle. Learn what is right for your car.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brake pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly toward the floor.
Pump the brake pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, you may have a leak or another brake system problem.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection test, you will:

options.text: Show that you know how to do a pre-trip inspection.
Watch someone else check your vehicle.
Watch a video on how to inspect a vehicle.
Change all the tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you know how to do a pre-trip inspection.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: When checking mirrors, you should:

options.text: Stare at the mirror for a long time.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Look at mirrors quickly when checking them. If you stare too long, you may travel far down the road without seeing what is ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, slow down. Use low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your hazard lights. Never speed up in fog.

questions.question: When going downhill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: As you go downhill and pick up speed.

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. If you don't, your brakes may overheat and fail.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Change each time you do it.
Follow the same order every time.
Only be done on sunny days.
Be skipped if the vehicle seems fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Use the same steps in the same order before every drive. This helps you remember all the steps and prevents you from skipping anything.

questions.question: Hazardous material placards must be at least:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10.75 inches square.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Can happen with just a little water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen with just a little water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. You don't need much water for this to happen.

questions.question: Which condition most likely causes hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely with worn tire tread or low tire pressure on wet roads. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: When visibility is low, such as at dawn or dusk, you should:
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts means they may be loose. Check them before you drive.

questions.question: Why should you do a pre-trip inspection in the same order each time?

options.text: You are less likely to forget something.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Following the same steps in the same order helps you remember what to check. This way, you won't skip anything.

questions.question: In cold weather, bridges freeze:

options.text: At the same time as other road surfaces.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Be extra careful on bridges and overpasses when driving in cold, wet conditions.

questions.question: Using a helper when backing up a large vehicle is:
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you have limited visibility. Use a helper to watch your blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact to communicate with them.

questions.explanation: Move out of their way if possible. Do not make eye contact, as it may anger them. Don't react to their actions.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
questions.explanation: Follow posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down for bad road or weather conditions. Slow down even more if workers are present.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The test may include these maneuvers: backing straight, offset parking (front and back), parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Do not base your gear shift decision on:
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speedometer. Learn which speeds work for each gear. Do not shift based on what other drivers are doing.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, it helps to:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible and finish quickly.
Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Walk around your vehicle first to check for hazards. Use both side mirrors while backing. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: Brake fade is caused by:
questions.explanation: Overusing brakes causes them to overheat and become less effective. This loss of braking power is called brake fade.

questions.question: Bridge height signs:
questions.explanation: Posted heights may not be correct. Clearance can change due to road repairs or snow buildup. Never assume a posted height is accurate.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:

options.text: Only required for hazardous material transport.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: How many licenses can a driver have?

options.text: Two licenses — one for cars and one for trucks.
One license for each state where they plan to drive.
A car license from one state and a CDL from another state.

questions.explanation: You can only have one driver's license. States share driver information in a computer system to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: When should you watch for black ice?

options.text: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When the temperature is above freezing and snow is on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it. Watch for black ice when it is below freezing and the road surface looks wet.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles enter the lane.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. If you did not see another vehicle before you start to move, the slow movement gives them time to react to your vehicle.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to get out of the way of other drivers.
Try not to use your mirrors.

questions.explanation: Backing up a large truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Use a helper if you can when backing up.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Look for an escape route like an escape ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Holds the spring brakes in place until they are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and the main air tank. It stops air from leaving the system if the compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: The time it takes to be ready to drive after sleeping.

questions.explanation: Sleep debt builds up when you do not sleep enough. You can only make up sleep debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, what should you do?

options.text: You can exceed it if passing another vehicle.
You can exceed it when driving in a rural area.

questions.explanation: A posted speed limit is the maximum speed you can drive under perfect conditions. Always slow down as road conditions require. Never exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Why should mirrors show both the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Showing only the road would make the driver carsick.
Seeing part of your vehicle gives you a reference point.
It is illegal to show only the road in the mirrors.
You need to see other vehicles reflected on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing part of your vehicle gives you a reference point.
questions.explanation: Part of your vehicle should be visible in your mirrors. This gives you a reference point to judge how close other drivers and objects are to your vehicle.

questions.question: When you apply your brakes, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle pulls to one side.
The vehicle does not pull to either side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle does not pull to either side.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when you brake, this is a sign of a brake problem.

questions.question: When a train is approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.
questions.explanation: Never try to cross before a train. Train speeds are hard to judge. If a train is approaching the crossing, stop and wait for it to pass completely before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: After cargo is secured on a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not let others inspect the cargo.

questions.explanation: Check cargo before the trip starts, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: If a heavy load is slowing your vehicle down, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle in second gear.

questions.explanation: The right lane is for slower vehicles. If your heavy load slows you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: A header board is used to:

options.text: Allow a driver to see behind them.
Protect the driver from moving cargo.
Prevent the driver from leaving the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from moving cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board, also called a "headache rack," protects the driver from cargo that moves during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When parallel parking on the driver's side, you should:

options.text: Pull forward directly into the space.
Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on the left. Then back into it while getting as close as possible to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: Which is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, heavy eyelids, repeated yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits, drifting from your lane, following too closely, and feeling irritable.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should inspect the windshield. Which is NOT something you should do?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check the windshield for cracks or problems that block your view. Check wiper arms for proper spring tension. Check wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and if they are secure.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to save time.
Is a distraction to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a distraction to the driver.
questions.explanation: Eating while driving distracts you. It takes your attention away from driving and requires you to remove one hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring during inspection, what happens?

options.text: The driver can drive at reduced speeds.
The vehicle will be put out-of-service until fixed.
The vehicle is fine since most of the spring is intact.
The driver must decrease the load weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will be put out-of-service until fixed.
questions.explanation: If at least one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, the vehicle must be taken out-of-service until the spring is repaired.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be on an uphill slope.
Should be on a downhill slope.
Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.
